keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria lacks the Blemmyes). "By the late 4th century, the Blemmyes had occupied Lower Nubia and established a kingdom"; they are an "Eastern Desert people". Torok is quoted as doubting "that there ever existed one centralised Blemmyan kingdom", so the shape is soft. No area on the page; Lower Nubia plus the Egyptian Red Sea governorate is my reading. [fx-26, F084/F100: the whole Red Sea Governorate (423 cells) and 13 Aswan cells were also drawn as Roman Egypt in every Roman shape 380-443, and the size rule gave them to the Blemmyes. Berenike (23.9 N) was a Roman port in the 4th century and 'formed an entire district with its own prefect' (Berenice Troglodytica page); Diocletian's peace of 298 moved the border 'north to Philae' (Blemmyes page) and the Blemmyes page gives no Blemmye control of the Red Sea coast, only early sources that place them 'in the Eastern Desert'. The Blemmye land is therefore Lower Nubia and the Eastern Desert south of the Roman strip. The Roman shapes are kept.]

Silko is dated "c. 5th century" and the Blemmyes page has Phonen ruling "c. 450": the year is a bridge.

wars.name: Silko's war against the Blemmyes
wars.outcome: Nobatian victory; the Blemmyes driven into the Eastern Desert, according to Silko's own inscription at Kalabsha.
wars.note: Silko is "c. 5th century"; the page gives no year.

certainty.note: Nomadic Eastern Desert people; the Nile holdings are known only from the 298 treaty and later inscriptions.

sources.title: Blemmyes
sources.note: Lower Nubia occupied and a kingdom established by the late 4th century, Kalabsha as capital, kings Tamal and Phonen (c. 450), Roman wars 193-298, the 298 treaty with Diocletian. No infobox, no area.

sources.title: Silko
sources.note: Silko of Nobatia (c. 5th century) defeated the Blemmyes to the north and claims at Kalabsha to have driven them into the Eastern Desert; no date.

sources.title: Berenice Troglodytica
sources.note: fx-26 (F084, F100): 'In the 4th century Berenice had again become an active port'; 'Under the Roman administration, Berenice itself formed an entire district with its own prefect'; periods 'Ptolemaic Kingdom to Byzantine Empire', abandoned after the 6th century. Berenike (about 23.9 N) was a Roman port on the Red Sea coast in the 4th century; the page does not mention the Blemmyes.

notes:
New dossier, thin: Cliopatria lacks the Blemmyes. Pages opened: Blemmyes, Silko (2). The Blemmyes page has no infobox and no dated territory except 'by the late 4th century ... occupied Lower Nubia and established a kingdom' and the Roman wars 193-298; the end is known only through Silko's undated Kalabsha inscription (Nobatia page of af-01-a: 450, confidence 1). Both start (380) and end (450) are placeholders at confidence 1. Disagreements: the Kingdom of Kush dossier has Kush take the Dodekaschoinos in 298 while the Blemmyes page has Rome treat with Nobatae and Blemmyes in 298 (Diocletian 'withdrawing to Philae'); the Nobatia dossier has the Nobatae in Lower Nubia from 347 (Cliopatria) while the Blemmyes page has them there by the late 4th century. The Beja (the Blemmyes' descendants, 'generally accepted') after 450 are a separate gap (af-01-a suggested a dossier 'beja', 700-1500). Gazetteer names needed: Kalabsha (Talmis, about 23.97 N 32.87 E, Lake Nasser).
Pre-kingdom conflicts of the people, not listed as a war because they lie before 380: 250 Decius, 253 attack on the Thebaid, 265 Firmus, 273 Palmyra, 279-280 Probus ('occupation of the Thebais'), 298 Diocletian's peace with the Nobatae and Blemmyes (Rome 'would move its borders north to Philae and pay both tribes an annual gold stipend'), all from the Blemmyes page.
